verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission concluded on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Floating in the Pacific Ocean on Friday... Artemis II mission began on April 1'; R2: 'Splashdown is targeted for 8:07 p.m. EDT... Flight Day 10'; R3: '11:22 pm ET April 10, 2026'; R5: 'April 10, 2026'; R8: 'April 10, 2026 · 5:07 p.m. PT Splashdown successful'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources explicitly state splashdown and mission conclusion on April 10, 2026, matching launch on April 1 for ~10-day mission.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission concluded with a successful splashdown in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Floating in the Pacific Ocean... off San Diego'; R2: 'Splashdown... off the coast of San Diego'; R3: 'splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego'; R5: 'off the coast of San Diego, California'; R8: 'splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California'
verifications.reasoning: All relevant sources confirm successful splashdown in Pacific Ocean off San Diego coast.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II splashdown occurred at 8:07 p.m. ET.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'After splashdown, at 8:07 p.m. Eastern time'; R2: 'Splashdown is targeted for 8:07 p.m. EDT'; R3: 'splashdown... at 8:07 p.m. EDT'; R4: 'pinpointed the exact splashdown time at 8:07 p.m. ET'; R8: '8:07 p.m.'
verifications.reasoning: Exact time 8:07 p.m. ET/EDT repeatedly stated across sources.

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule landed safely in the water.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'successful conclusion... splashdown'; R2: 'Orion will splash down... completing the Artemis II crew’s return'; R3: 'flawless splashdown'; R4: 'safely splashed down'; R8: 'Splashdown successful!'
verifications.reasoning: Sources uniformly describe safe, successful water splashdown.

verifications.claim: A joint NASA and U.S. Navy recovery team extracted the four crew members.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'recovery team... U.S.S. John P. Murtha... helped the astronauts out'; R2: 'combined NASA and U.S. military recovery team will be standing by... extract the crew'; R3: 'U.S. Navy sailors... Navy dive team assists Artemis II crew'; R4: 'NASA and U.S. Navy recovery teams'
verifications.reasoning: Explicit mentions of joint NASA/Navy teams extracting crew.

verifications.claim: The splashdown location was the Pacific Ocean west of San Diego.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Pacific Ocean... waters off San Diego'; R2: 'Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego'; R3: 'Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego'; R5: 'off the coast of San Diego, California'
verifications.reasoning: Sources specify Pacific off San Diego coast; 'west' is precise as San Diego faces Pacific westward, directly supported.

verifications.reasoning: Consistent description as ~10-day crewed lunar flyby.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew faced extreme heat during reentry
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: 'heat enveloping the spacecraft... temperatures... during re-entry'; R2: 'temperatures of about 3,000 degrees Fahrenheit'; R3: 'superheat gas... 3,000 degrees Fahrenheit'; R4: 'Temperatures can be up to 5,000 degrees Fahrenheit'
verifications.reasoning: Sources detail extreme external heat on spacecraft during reentry (3000-5000°F), but focus on capsule/heat shield; crew experiences G-forces inside, so 'crew faced' is broader interpretation.
